editorial_intro: Spider-Man: Brand New Day sits at roughly $856M domestic — within striking distance of The Force Awakens' all-time record of $936.7M — and has crossed $2.1B worldwide, only the eighth film in history to join the $2B club. The Odyssey glides past $540M domestic and $1.4B worldwide, officially Christopher Nolan's biggest film ever. This weekend, Insidious: Out of the Further opened at #2 with ~$25M on an $18M budget — the franchise's formula still prints money. In Bollywood, Awarapan 2 has surged past ₹189 Cr worldwide, making it Emraan Hashmi's biggest solo hit by a mile. Suriya's Vishwanath & Sons crossed ₹150 Cr worldwide in just eight days. Batwara 1947 reached ₹52 Cr but is struggling against its massive budget. A24's Bourdain biopic Tony (95% RT) and Mubi's Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma (95% RT) are the indie darlings of the month. Coming this week: Yash's long-awaited Toxic arrives Aug 26.

movies.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
movies.why_watch: Only the eighth film in history to cross $2B worldwide, and it got there faster than everything except Endgame. $856M domestic and climbing — it's genuinely chasing The Force Awakens' all-time record. Tom Holland and Zendaya's fourth MCU Spider-Man picks up years after No Way Home erased Peter Parker from memory. 90% critics, 98% audience. Still the biggest movie on the planet by a wide margin.

movies.title: The Odyssey
movies.why_watch: $540M domestic and over $1.4B worldwide — now Christopher Nolan's highest-grossing film ever, surpassing The Dark Knight Rises. Shot entirely with IMAX 70mm cameras, a first in cinema history. IMAX's best-selling release of all time, with some 70mm screenings sold out through September. Matt Damon's Odysseus is getting serious Oscar buzz. 94% critics, 97% audience. If you haven't seen it in IMAX yet, this is the movie that format was built for.

movies.title: Insidious: Out of the Further
movies.why_watch: Opened at #2 this weekend with ~$25M on an $18M budget — the Insidious franchise just keeps printing money. The sixth entry flips the script: Amelia Eve plays a mother who can pull spirits out of the Further, and when the demons realize her power, things get ugly. Lin Shaye returns as Elise Rainier. 58% RT — the best-reviewed Insidious since the 2010 original. Not groundbreaking horror, but a solid scare machine for franchise fans.

movies.title: Awarapan 2
movies.why_watch: ₹189 Cr worldwide and still climbing — Emraan Hashmi's biggest solo hit ever, by a massive margin. ₹22 Cr opening day, ₹82 Cr opening weekend, and it dominated the Independence Day clash. The sequel to the 2007 cult classic that defined Hashmi's brooding romantic-hero era. Music by Mithoon. Mixed reviews haven't dented the audience turnout one bit — nostalgia and the Awarapan brand are doing all the heavy lifting.

movies.title: Vishwanath & Sons
movies.why_watch: ₹150 Cr worldwide in just eight days — Suriya's fastest film to cross ₹100 Cr and his fastest to hit $1M in North America. A warm family romance with Suriya as a 40-year-old champion shooter and Mamitha Baiju as his younger love interest. ₹86 Cr India net and ₹51 Cr overseas — the international numbers are unusually strong. Raveena Tandon returns to Tamil cinema. Cleaning up in Tamil and Telugu markets and headed well past ₹175 Cr.

movies.title: Batwara 1947
movies.why_watch: Sunny Deol and Rajkumar Santoshi's partition epic opened slow at ₹5.75 Cr but spiked on Independence Day. ₹52 Cr worldwide in 10 days — respectable, but tough math against its reported budget. Produced by Aamir Khan, music by A.R. Rahman. Preity Zinta returns to Hindi cinema after an eight-year hiatus. Word of mouth is warm — if you care about partition stories told with craft, catch it before it loses screens to Toxic this week.

movies.title: The End of Oak Street
movies.why_watch: What if your suburban street got ripped from the earth and dropped into a prehistoric world full of dinosaurs? From It Follows director David Robert Mitchell. Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor fight to keep their family alive. 83% on RT. Took a 62% second-weekend dip, which is a shame — this is the best dinosaur movie since Jurassic Park. The most interesting non-franchise film of August, and one that deserves a bigger audience.

movies.title: Tony
movies.why_watch: 95% on Rotten Tomatoes. A24's biopic of Anthony Bourdain follows a 19-year-old Bourdain taking a summer restaurant job in Provincetown in 1975 and discovering his calling. Dominic Sessa channels the raw energy of young Bourdain, and Antonio Banderas as his mentor chef is reportedly electric. Now playing wide after expanding from limited release. If you love food, travel, or just a great coming-of-age story, this is the best-reviewed film in theaters right now alongside Camp Miasma.

movies.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
movies.why_watch: 95% on RT with 227 reviews and an 89 on Metacritic — one of the best-reviewed films of 2026, period. Jane Schoenbrun's meta-slasher about a queer filmmaker hired to reboot a horror franchise, who becomes obsessed with the original's reclusive star (Gillian Anderson, absolutely sublime). Won the Queer Palm at Cannes. Pushed the Angelika in New York to its best weekend since Wes Anderson's The Phoenician Scheme. Not your typical horror — it's funny, intimate, and wildly personal.

movies.title: Toy Story 5
movies.why_watch: $476M+ domestic in ten weeks — well past Toy Story 4's total. Pixar made the toys fight an iPad and somehow delivered their most emotionally devastating film since the incinerator scene. 93% critics, 94% audience. Showtimes are thinning against the blockbuster onslaught, but still the best family option in theaters if you haven't caught it yet.

movies.title: Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups
movies.why_watch: Yash's first film since KGF: Chapter 2 grossed ₹1,200 Cr worldwide. After four postponements, Toxic finally arrives Aug 26 — timed to hit the Onam/Eid/Raksha Bandhan corridor. Directed by National Award winner Geetu Mohandas, this period gangster drama was shot simultaneously in Kannada and English for global audiences. Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, and Tara Sutaria round out the cast. The most anticipated Indian release of the week. Opens Tuesday, Aug 26.
